title: What is an Ig Nobel Prize?
summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the Ig Nobel Prizes, the parody awards that honor unusual but genuine scientific research, held at Harvard and webcast around October 1 (the hosts mention a live webcast at 7:15 Eastern). They explain the ten categories, the Improbable Research magazine behind the awards, and the nomination process. They recount the Air Force "gay bomb" and other non-lethal chemical projects that won the 2007 Ig Nobel Peace Prize, the controversy when UK science minister Bob May criticized the awards and told them not to honor British scientists, and a run of past winners (soggy cereal, MRI of intercourse, necrophiliac ducks, Coca-Cola as spermicide, woodpecker headaches, mindless eating soup bowl, group photo eyes closed, jet lag in hamsters and Viagra, digital rectal massage for hiccups, stripper tips and ovulation). The episode closes with a listener mail segment naming the biggest badass of World War II, where listeners favored Simo Häyhä, the Finnish sniper nicknamed White Death, over Audie Murphy, and credits several listeners.
topics: biggest badass of World War II

segments.title: Opening banter and Darwin Awards
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about the August heat, then mention the upcoming Ig Nobel Awards and contrast them with the Darwin Awards.

segments.title: What the Ig Nobel Prizes are
segments.summary: The hosts explain the name as a riff on the Nobel Prize and 'ignoble', describe the ten categories, the nomination process, and Mark Abrams' stance on the awards.

segments.title: Air Force gay bomb and 2007 Peace Prize
segments.summary: The Air Force-funded research into harassing and non-lethal chemicals, including the so-called gay bomb, which won the 2007 Ig Nobel Peace Prize; the Air Force did not show up to accept.

segments.title: Ceremony and judges
segments.summary: Discussion of who judges the awards, including Nobel laureates and celebrities, the Harvard ceremony, one-minute speeches, and Little Miss Cutie Pie.

segments.title: Bob May and British controversy
segments.summary: UK science minister Bob May criticized the awards and told organizers not to honor British scientists after the soggy cereal study; his successor attended in 2002.

segments.title: Notable past winners
segments.summary: Run through of past winners: MRI video of intercourse, necrophiliac ducks, Coca-Cola as spermicide, woodpecker headaches, mindless eating soup bowl, group photo eyes closed, hamsters with Viagra and jet lag, and digital rectal massage for hiccups.

segments.title: Strippers and ovulation study
segments.summary: The economics prize went to a study finding strippers earn more tips when ovulating; the hosts wrap up the Ig Nobel discussion.

segments.title: Biggest badass of World War II
segments.summary: Listeners respond to the earlier challenge; the hosts pick Simo Häyhä, the Finnish sniper known as White Death, over Audie Murphy, crediting listeners Carson, Timman, Devon, and Adrian. Closing ad reads follow.
topics: biggest badass of World War II
